source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.short_quote: each of the benefics, Jupiter and Venus, takes seven degrees; the malefics, Saturn and Mars, take five degrees each; and Mercury, being of common influence, takes six degrees

prerequisites: Ptolemaic exaltation, triplicity, and house rulerships
rulerships for the current sign and the next two signs

condition.precondition: no planet has two rights of dominion in the same sign or in the next two signs

normalized_rule: For the Ptolemaic base terms, when no planet has a double right in the current sign or the next two signs, assign seven degrees each to Jupiter and Venus, five each to Saturn and Mars, and six degrees to Mercury.
synthesis_notes: This is a deterministic allocation within the Ptolemaic traditional scheme, not an astronomical measurement or empirical probability statement.
review_notes: Keep this Ptolemaic allocation source-specific. Chapter XXIII's Egyptian and Chaldaic distributions are separate variants and are represented by separate candidates and an active conflict; do not flatten them into this rule.
transmission_notes: Ashmand's Chapter XXIII presents Egyptian and Chaldaic methods before Chapter XXIV gives the Ptolemaic method. This candidate is limited to the Ptolemaic base allocation; certainty is scoped to the cited Ashmand/Proclus transmission.
